chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: Hammond's CBS Jam Session and the Nineteenth Hole
summary: Mosley takes part in a linked CBS blues broadcast and Hammond brings Krupa's trombonists to the Nineteenth Hole.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: It's a shame, you should have had a lot of air checks made during that time; were you doing any broadcasting?

No I wasn't broadcasting. I was a guest. Johnny Hammond was a moderator on a thing called Jam Session on CBS, and he had me as his guest. One night--Benny would remember this--Benny Goodman was in Boston, another band in Chicago and we were here in New York, in the studio, CBS studio, and we all played the blues. Johnny Hammond was the moderator, and we all played the blues and it came out on the air as if we were in one place, and this guy--what's this guy playing the piano?

Oscar Levant. Oscar Levant was playing piano-- anyway it was on Jam Session, we did the blues. That was after Johnny had come out to Barnes Tavern and he got really in my corner and one night after we got down to a place called the Nineteenth Hole--
He brought Gene Krupa's whole trombone section down there one night.
That's funny, because I would imagine that you would have had some offers at that time, probably some of the white bands would have wanted you to go with them.
I did, but I had enough playing with anybody else's band. I had been with
the best, as far as the name was concerned, and I didn't want to get back in with being with anybody else at that time.
